headline: Promoter Group Consortium Files SEBI Takeover Disclosure for Dish TV India
sum: A promoter consortium including Direct Media Distribution Ventures, Veena Investments, and related entities and individuals filed a mandatory disclosure under SEBI's Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations, signalling a structural reorganisation or acquisition within the Dish TV group. The filing suggests a material move in shareholding architecture or control among existing promoters.
implication: Reg 31(4) disclosure is mandatory when persons acting in concert effect or propose a substantial acquisition; this filing flags potential concert-party acquisition mechanics and triggers formal review of shareholding patterns, disclosure timelines and open-offer conditionality under SEBI Takeover Code.
detail: The disclosure filed with NSE on 23–24 Jun 2026 involves a multi-party consortium comprising corporate vehicles (Direct Media Distribution Ventures, Veena Investments, World Crest Advisors, JSGG Infra Developers), a Mauritius-resident holding company (Agrani Holdings), and individual promoters (Gaurav Goel, Priti Poddar, Jai Goel, Jawahar Lal Goel, Nishi Goel, Suryansh Goel, Sushila Devi). The filing is lodged under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, which requires disclosure of concert-party acquisitions or acquisition proposals. No consideration, target shareholding or timeline for completion is disclosed in the NSE filing; further details may be in the full disclosure Form, underlying SPA, or subsequent stock-exchange announcements.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of concert-party or substantial acquisition proposals; defines triggering events, disclosure timing (within 2 days of board approval or execution of binding agreement), and concert-party definition.
Definition of 'acquisition' (shares, voting rights, control); threshold triggers (25%, 35%, 55% and key operational milestones); applicability to acquisition proposals.
Open offer conditionality: if acquisition results in trigger threshold, open offer to public shareholders is mandatory (unless exempted); timing, price-setting, acceptances.
Concert-party definition and deemed concert-party persons; common object test; disclosure obligations of all concert parties and each party's individual shareholding.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 5, 8 (private company definition); Section 89 (preferential allotment), Section 62 (board approval for new share issuance)
framework.note: If acquisition is funded by fresh allotment to consortium members, preferential allotment route and board/shareholder approvals required; disclosure in board minutes and MCA filing.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 30, Schedule III
framework.note: Continuous disclosure obligation for material acquisition proposals and changes in shareholding; Regulation 30(5) – material event disclosure within 2 days.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 & Rules — Sections 4, 6
framework.note: If Agrani Holdings (Mauritius) is acquiring or investing, FDI limits (100% under automatic route in broadcasting), repatriation rules, and RBI approval (if over threshold) applicable.

framework.ref: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting — Press Information Bureau guidance on control changes in broadcasting entities
framework.note: Dish TV holds broadcasting licence/carriage agreements; material change in control may trigger PIB/MIB clearance or intimation; indirect foreign control (Agrani Holdings) may require additional scrutiny.

structure.novel: Multi-tier consortium structure combining domestic corporate vehicles (World Crest Advisors, JSGG Infra), private investments (Direct Media Distribution, Veena Investments), overseas holding company (Agrani Holdings, Mauritius), and individual promoters (Goel family, Priti Poddar, Sushila Devi); suggests possible club-deal restructuring or intra-promoter consolidation masked by concert-party acquisition framework.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 31(4)
triggers.note: Trigger: concert-party acquisition proposal requiring mandatory disclosure within 2 days of board/binding agreement.
If acquisition results in 25%+, 35%+, or control threshold, open offer is mandatory unless exempted (e.g., inter-se transfer among promoters).
Agrani Holdings (Mauritius) involvement triggers FDI review; broadcasting sector allows 100% FDI (automatic), but repatriation and control issues may require RBI/FIPB intimation.
